newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index ends up on active foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index ends up on active foreign buying.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed up on Friday following active foreign buying of selected big-capitalised stocks, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 3.43 points, or 0.61 percent, to close at 568.99 points. Gainers led losers by 64 to 40, with 50 counters unchanged.
"There is a potential for market to move up slightly in the coming week with the positive news of corporate actions available in the market," Jordan Zulkarnain, analyst of Pentasena Securities, said.
The market already had anticipated the possible hike of U.S.interest rate, Zulkarnain said.
"I expect foreing buying to continue in selected stocks," he said.
Lippo group's financial units, Lippo Life, Lippo Securities and Lippo Bank of Lippo Group were actively traded following the announcement of plans to sweeten the terms of its restructuring plan.

Lippo Life topped the active list with 9.1 million shares traded, fell 25 rupiah to 2,025 after rose to 2,100 rupiah in morning session. Brokers said the fall was due to profit taking after early gains.
Car maker Astra International rose 175 rupiah to 3,300 rupiah on 8.2 million shares on talk that another conglomerate was likely to buy stake in the company.
But Suharto, a broker of local firm Bhakti Investama, said even without the rumours, Astra's price was quite cheap.
"It has good fundamentals and its quite cheap. There is no reason not to buy," he added.
Well-diversified firm Bakrie Brothers rose 250 rupiah to 3,225 rupiah on 1.5 million shares.
Brokers said the rise was due to fresh buying after the company's better-than-expected first half year result.
